sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: The HAEWI-2FLAG construct was used in co-immunoprecipitation and surface-biotinylation experiments in CHO cells; surface display of the related EWI-2FLAG construct was confirmed by surface biotinylation (L3). Direct surface detection of the HA epitope itself was not separately quantified in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: The paper explicitly constructs a full-length, membrane-anchored EWI-2 with an HA tag placed immediately after the signal peptide, placing it at the extracellular N-terminus. The authoritative topology gives SP = 1–27 (A27 is the last SP residue, R28 is the mature N-terminus), so the junction is insert_after_residue=27. The paper's stated SP boundary (1–25) differs by two residues from the computed topology; we use the authoritative landmark (27) and note the discrepancy. No residue number is stated in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived. The extracellular domain spans 28–579, placing this tag far (>550 residues) from the TM boundary. Full-length human EWI-2 (IGSF8) construct pcDNA3.1/HAEWI-2FLAG encodes the EWI-2 signal peptide followed immediately by the HA9 epitope (YPYDVPDYA) fused to the entire EWI-2FLAG sequence, expressed in mammalian cells. The paper states the signal peptide spans aa 1–25; the authoritative computed topology places the SP at 1–27 (cleavage after A27, mature N-terminus R28). The paper names no specific junction residue — only 'after signal peptide' — and exactly one extracellular terminus exists, so the junction is topology-derived at insert_after_residue=27.

sources.claim: Plasmid pcDNA3.1/wint-FLAG encoding EWI-2 signal peptide (amino acids 1–25) and EWI-2 amino acids 166–613 fused to FLAG tag was made by fusion-PCR from template pcDNA3.1/EWI-2FLAG. pcDNA3.1/HAEWI-2FLAG encodes EWI-2 signal peptide followed by HA9 epitope (YPYDVPDYA) tag fused to the entire sequence of EWI-2FLAG.

literature_notes: Four ledger lines were evaluated. L2 grounds the single extracellular surface site: an HA tag inserted after the signal peptide at the N-terminus of full-length membrane-anchored EWI-2 (IGSF8). L1 and L3 describe a C-terminal FLAG tag on EWI-2; the C-terminus (residue 613) falls within the intracellular tail (603–613) and is therefore not a surface tag site — recorded in other_positions. L4 describes a C-terminal GFP fusion, likewise intracellular — also recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for IGSF8. The paper's stated signal peptide length (1–25) differs by two residues from the authoritative computed topology (1–27); the junction is placed at residue 27 per the authoritative landmarks, and the discrepancy is noted in the rationale. Confidence is medium because the HA-tag surface display was not directly demonstrated for the HAEWI-2FLAG construct specifically (L3 confirms surface display only for the C-terminal FLAG construct).

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length EWI-2 (EWI-2FLAG); residue 613 lies within the intracellular tail (603–613), confirmed by surface biotinylation of the extracellular domain but the tag itself faces the cytoplasm.
C-terminal GFP fusion of full-length EWI-2 (pDest-C-GFP vector); residue 613 is the last intracellular residue, so the GFP faces the cytoplasm.
